newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen continuing recent strength.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen continuing recent strength.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures are called to open sharply higher Tuesday, continuing its recent strength based on rising cash market prices in the West.
"PV (Palo Verde prices) is supported by the heat in the Southwest, and COB (California-Oregon Border prices) is just following PV," said a West Coast electricity dealer.
In the Southwest, the Phoenix-Tucson area is expected to see temperatures in the mid-90s F today.

In over-the-counter (OTC) business, June COB futures were quoted at $15.75-16.05 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Monday's settlement of $15.45, and June PV at $21.80-22.00 against previous day's close of $21.38.
The June OTC prices also surpassed the life-of-contract highs set during Monday's regular session.
Day-ahead electricity prices at COB and PV were generally 50 to $1 higher than Monday in early trading, traders said.

Short-term physical power prices continued their recent climb due to plant outages, firm air-conditioning demand in thw Southwest and lack of daily peak-hour supply from Bonneville Power Administration (BPA),

Generation capacity in the western U.S. remained limited, with about 8,000 megawatts in the West said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of the idled capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
Restart of the 550 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired power complex in Wyoming was delayed to tomorrow from Sunday.
In the Northwest, temperatures would average above normal Wednesday through Sunday, while readings would run six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
